chunks: From him, from one of those who narrated it, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) forbade picking teeth with pomegranate stems, myrtle leaves, and reeds, and said: 'These stir the vein of the eater.'

key_terms.الرُّمَّان: Pomegranate (specifically its stem used as a toothpick)
key_terms.عِرْق: Vein / root (referring to the gum tissue)

ai.seo_question: What materials are forbidden for picking teeth in Shia hadith and why?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the Prophetic emphasis on *Sunnah* practices of dental hygiene, specifically cautioning against using rigid materials like pomegranate stems and reeds that may irritate the gums by 'stirring the vein.' In Shia jurisprudence, this is often interpreted as a recommendation for *Istihbab* (preferability) of using softer, flexible twigs like *Siwak* (Arak tree) to preserve gum health and prevent bleeding, reflecting the broader Islamic principle of preserving bodily well-being (*Hifz al-Sihha*).
